standard_prerequisites.name: Differential graded algebras and bimodules
standard_prerequisites.statement: Dg R-algebras (A,d), (B,d), (C,d), and dg (A,B)- and (B,C)-bimodules, with their homotopy and derived categories D(-,d).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the statement (source lines 5960-5964).

standard_prerequisites.name: Derived tensor product of bimodules
standard_prerequisites.statement: The left derived functor - tensor^L_A N on D(A,d) defined by the construction of the chapter, together with its functoriality in the bimodule up to quasi-isomorphism.
standard_prerequisites.use: The two functors being composed and the announced N'' are derived tensor functors (source lines 5965-5974, 5978-5982).

standard_prerequisites.name: Property (P) for bimodules and its filtration sequences
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every dg bimodule has a quasi-isomorphic representative with property (P), carrying an admissible filtration whose graded pieces are direct sums of shifts of the free bimodule, and a split admissible short exact sequence displaying the filtration (the author's lemmas lemma-bimodule-resolve and lemma-bimodule-property-P-sequence, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: Both reduction chains of the proof run along these filtrations (source lines 5980-5982, 5992-6024, 6035-6051).

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the derived tensor functor
standard_prerequisites.statement: The derived tensor functor is exact as a functor of triangulated categories, commutes with direct sums, and transforms admissible exact sequences of complexes into admissible exact sequences (the author's lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what licenses the two reductions (source lines 5988-6018).

core_obligations: Reduce to property (P) representatives: replace N and N' by quasi-isomorphic bimodules with property (P) using functoriality of the construction in the bimodule (source lines 5977-5982).

Identify the composite: show that the lemma holds with N'' = N tensor_B N', which by the general comparison lemma reduces to the statement that N_B tensor^L_B N' to (N tensor_B N')_C is an isomorphism in D(C,d) (source lines 5982-5990).

Run the first reduction: use the split admissible sequence for the property-(P) filtration of N, the induced distinguished triangle in D(B,d) and the exactness of the derived tensor functor to reduce to a single filtration piece, and then to (A tensor_R B)_B (source lines 5991-6032).

Run the second reduction and conclude: resolve (A tensor_R B)_B by a property-(P) module P, filter N' the same way to reduce to a graded piece _B(B tensor_R C)_C, and observe that the remaining map represents the isomorphism assumed in the statement (source lines 6034-6063).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to property-(P) bimodules, set N'' = N tensor_B N' and reduce to one comparison map in D(C,d).
Use the filtration of N, the induced distinguished triangle and exactness to reduce to the single case (A tensor_R B)_B.
Resolve (A tensor_R B)_B with a property-(P) module and reduce along the filtration of N' to one graded piece.
Identify the remaining map with the assumed isomorphism (equation-plain-versus-derived-algebras) and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general-algebra at source lines 5958-5975: for differential graded R-algebras (A,d), (B,d), (C,d), a dg (A,B)-bimodule N and a dg (B,C)-bimodule N', and under the standing assumption that the comparison map (equation-plain-versus-derived-algebras) is an isomorphism, the composition of the two derived tensor functors -tensor^L_A N and -tensor^L_B N' is isomorphic to -tensor^L_A N'' for the (A,C)-bimodule N'' = N tensor_B N' described in the proof. The proof at source lines 5977-6064 is a long reduction: first replace both bimodules by property-(P) representatives, then use the split admissible short exact sequences of the property-(P) filtrations and the exactness of the derived tensor functor on the resulting distinguished triangles to reduce the claim to a single graded piece, then resolve (A tensor_R B)_B by a property-(P) module and repeat the reduction along a second filtration, ending on the one map that by construction represents the assumed isomorphism. Nothing in the argument is deep, but the two nested reduction chains are what makes the lemma hard to read, and the statement itself only asserts the existence of the bimodule N''.
